01 · Summary

All it involves.

What we do

We write our reports and materials as a web page instead of a PowerPoint file, and publish them as a link.

With what
Claudewrites and builds the file.
GitHubstores it.
Vercelputs it online.
Supabaseadds the database behind comments and access.
Google Cloudregisters the Google sign-in of the price list.
What it costs
Claude only
paid subscription · the rest on free plans

Nothing beyond the Claude subscription. GitHub, Vercel and Supabase are used on their free plans.

What we get

A report that opens on any device, updates in minutes, and never needs to be redesigned.

Where we want to go

Ideally an internal AI solution we can train on our own needs and run in a controlled environment — an AI TOP ATOM — so we can extend all of this while our business information never leaves the company.

02 · The tools

What each tool is, and what it does for us.

CLAUDE

AI assistant

  • We hand it a prepared extract — never the source files.
  • Builds the HTML file applying our own style rules.
  • Applies corrections as edits, without rebuilding the file.
How we use it

We open a chat, hand over the prepared figures and the structure, and it returns the finished file.

GITHUB

Where the file lives

  • Stores the report file.
  • Keeps every previous version automatically.
  • Lets us fix data directly in the browser.
How we use it

We paste the updated file over the old one. Nothing is ever lost.

VERCEL

What puts it online

  • Turns the GitHub file into a working web address.
  • Updates the live page whenever the file changes.
  • Keeps every deploy, so we can roll back to any version.
How we use it

We connect it once per report. After that it publishes on its own.

Other tools

Only when the report has to do more than be read

SUPABASE

The database behind the report: comments with replies, and access codes checked on the server — never written inside the file.

GOOGLE CLOUD

Where the Google sign-in of the price list is registered, so access can be tied to a corporate account.

03 · The workflow

Which tool we use at each step.

Six steps, always in the same order. The first one has no AI in it.

1

Prepare

Us · no AI

We take from the source documents only the figures the report will publish, and put them into a single working file.

2

Brief

Claude

We hand over that working file and the section structure, pointing to where each figure sits: which slide, which structure.

3

Content

Claude

We agree the text of each section in the chat and validate the numbers. Nothing is built until this is closed.

4

Build

Claude

Claude generates the HTML file applying our style rules, structure and quality controls by using a created skill that compiles all this information.

5

Review

Claude

We send corrections by section number. Claude edits the existing file instead of making a new one.

6

Publish

GitHub + Vercel

The file goes to GitHub as index.html. Vercel turns it into a live link. Updates repeat steps 5 and 6 only.

Alternative for step 6

Step 6 can be done without GitHub. For example, Netlify publishes a dropped folder in one move — but then the file cannot be corrected in the browser, there is no history of what changed, and it lives on a single laptop.

04 · How it used to work

Five things that used to happen every time.

BeforeNow
1
Draft the deck, then decide what fits on a slide and what gets cut.
→
The detail lives under See more. Nothing is cut to make it fit.
2
Attach the backup data, or paste links people have to open one by one.
→
The figures read the source. There is no backup file to attach.
3
A meeting, because the deck alone does not answer the questions.
→
The questions are answered on the page: open the detail, or move the inputs.
4
A source document changes, so the deck has to be updated and re-sent.
→
The page is updated once. The link everyone already has is the new version.
5
English for HQ and Spanish for the team: two decks that sooner or later stopped matching.
→
One document, one button. And a PPT download for whoever still prefers the file.

07 · The price list portal

The same idea, taken to the channel.

Built by Antony Rios (Peruvian Sales Team) for GIGABYTE Peru resellers. Different publishing tools, same logic.

⤢

Netlify

Published by dropping the folder — no GitHub and no Vercel.

⤢

Supabase Auth

Google sign-in and email, with mandatory email confirmation.

⤢

Registered users

34 resellers to date. Names and emails covered for this report.

How it was built

Antony followed the same first five steps. Only step 6 changed: instead of GitHub + Vercel, the folder is dropped straight into Netlify, which stores and publishes in one move. He took that route to test a different way of publishing.

What it costs

Netlify's free tier covers about 20 redeploys a month, and the price list is republished every time a new list arrives — so it runs on the USD 9/month plan. The same portal could run on our six steps, on the free plans.

How access works
  1. Anyone can register with company, role and email.
  2. The price list stays hidden until a GIGABYTE executive approves the account.
  3. Inside, the reseller builds a cart and the quote is routed by WhatsApp to the executive of their department.
  4. An internal panel logs every quote and every sign-in.

The process does not depend on the tools. The five steps held; only the way of publishing changed.

08 · What we are asking for

One machine, four projects.

AI TOP ATOM, on our premises

Today the only thing we send to the AI is the set of figures the report is going to publish anyway. That rule is what makes the first three projects safe to build — and it is also what keeps them small: they can never touch our live data.

A machine of our own is how we keep the rule and lose the limit. The fourth one needs it outright: at the booth the agent answers from the catalogue itself, with no one preparing anything.

It does not replace what we use to build the reports. It adds what we cannot do today.
What the machine has to do
Run a language model locally, with no internet.
Take voice in and answer by voice.
Be fed with our own catalogue, prices and stock.
Work at the booth, and in the office, on the same box.
What it unlocks
01

Internal operating system

One platform, three views: the work, the delivery and the result, for accurate KPI follow-up.

02

Client budget portal

Each client sees their own allocation and its evidence.

03

Stock-driven campaign planning

Alerts on aging and incoming units, so we push the right model at the right moment.

04

The showroom agent

An AI assistant that turns our exhibitions into a brand experience.

Priority

We are not asking to keep doing the same. We are asking to do it with our own data, in our own house, and in front of the customer.
